newsitem.title: USA: Conrail and Union Pacific win ruling - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Conrail and Union Pacific win ruling - WSJ.

text.p: A ruling by the Federal Surface Transportation Board protects the right of Conrail Inc and Union Pacific Corp to set their own rates in three cases where utilities were each served by just one railroad in receiving shipments of coal, The Wall Street Journal reported Friday.
The case was brought in 1994 by three utilities against Conrail, Union Pacific and railroads now owned by Union Pacific, the story says.
The utilities wanted low freight rates that would let them use a competing railroad for part of their service, but claimed their primary railroads prevented that, the story says.
Many railroad customers are served by only one carrier, and the Association of American Railroads said an antirailroad ruling could have effected $2.4 billion in annual profits, the story says.
As a result of the ruling, industry watchers fear that frustrated railroad customers might seek stricter regulation of railroads, the story says.
